posts.t: Filoyell, Hey, thanks for stopping by. It would be very difficult to take a trade based on the information provided on your chart. We have to look further left to know what the low marked in the chart below is a reaction to. That low could very well have been the end of a retrace that hadn't yet hit a target, it could be a break into a PAZ, and it is also possible that it is an engulf of an entire zone. When I began RTM, I thought I could pick any random low or high, and a break of that level automatically means the FTR following that break was important. It is always important to look "left and then left again" to know what that low or high is a reaction to. Remember we are reading the entire market.

Hi Josh!

I would like to thank you for your posts. It seems that you understand this method very well and you are also good trader. So, if you don't mind, I'd like to ask you a few questions.

1. How long did it take to understand this method?

2. How much time do you spend by trading daily? 3. What is your frequency of trades? 4. What is your average RR?

I have to admit that I'm quite struggling with this method. I spent seven months by studying (every day), but I think it is really unique analytic approach which is not easy to learn. So, I need some assurance that somebody can trade like IF. That even I can handle it.

Thank you very much!

posts.t:
Deenius, I am still trying my hardest to fully understand this method. I have understood the core concept of RTM, but I'm still trying to apply the method to the charts. There are days I can open a chart, and read it perfectly clear, and then there are days I feel like I'm starting over from the very beginning. It is definitely a work in progress. I credit all of the success I've had so far to IF, and many other traders on here (Les Paul, Harry, Benhur, Smimon, Michal238, Jurij, Fader, etc) just to name a few. Now to answer your questions.

1. I'm still understanding this method. So I really jumped in and took learning serious about 9months ago. 2. I have a FT job so I trade HTF 1hour and higher. So I normally spend my time adjusting my charts to the price action from that day. 3. I find what I call high quality trades about 3-4 times a week, but that's going through all the charts. 4. My average RR is normally 1:10. I try to narrow my zones down as far as I can with clarity.

posts.t: Ok.. here is an explanation of the entry on that Audusd trade. I've really spent the last few weeks turning over every stone I can to really understand things. After going through countless of charts both here and on FF from IF and some of the other masters, I noticed something majority of the charts had in common. The QM. I use to think the QM was all in the eyes of the trader. I noticed many traders picking random highs and lows for their QM. It wasn't until I came across a post from IF that things really started to make sense. This trade was nearly identical to a trade IF took over 2 years ago, and I'm starting to see this happens quite often, and they are really high RR trades.
posts.fa: اوکی… اینجا توضیح ورود آن معاملهٔ Audusd است. واقعاً چند هفتهٔ گذشته همهٔ زوایا را گشتم تا واقعاً چیزها را بفهمم. بعد از مرور چارت‌های بی‌شمار هم این‌جا و هم روی FF از IF و بعضی استادان دیگر، متوجه شدم اکثریت چارت‌ها چه چیزی مشترک داشتند. QM. قبلاً فکر می‌کردم QM همه در چشم معامله‌گر است. متوجه شدم تریدران زیادی سقف‌ها و کف‌های تصادفی برای QM‌شان انتخاب می‌کردند. تا وقتی به پستی از If برخوردم، چیزها واقعاً شروع به معنا پیدا کردن کردند. این معامله تقریباً یکسان با معامله‌ای بود که If بیش از 2 سال پیش گرفته بود، و می‌بینم که این اتفاق نسبتاً زیاد می‌افتد، و واقعاً معامله‌های R:R بالایی هستند.
